Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1.
Mr. Gurmehar Sistani and Mr. B.M. Pingal, learned counsels for the petitioner.

2. Mr. Amarendra Pratap Singh, learned Additional Advocate General assisted by Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand/ respondent nos. 1 to 6.
3.

Mr. Devdutt Kamath, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. Vikas Bahuguna and Mr. Javed Un- Rehman, learned counsel for respondent nos. 7 to 9.
4.
Mr. B.S. Negi, learned counsel for respondent no.10.

5. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for respondent no. 11.
6.

The petitioner has preferred the present Writ Petition, statedly, in public interest, to seek the following reliefs :-
"i. Issue a writ of Certiorari or any other appropriate Writ, or order, or direction to set aside order dated 05.08.2023 passed by the Ld. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Uttarkashi in Crl.
Misc .
Case no. 152/2023 titled as "State through SI Prakash Rana vs Deepak Bijalwan&Ors".

entities.text: State through SI Prakash Rana vs Deepak Bijalwan&Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
ii. Quash the negative final report no. 25/2023 filed before Ld. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Uttarkashi in FIR no. 01/2023 under sections 406, 409, 120B and 420 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 registered at Police Station Kotwali Uttarkashi.
WPPIL/182/2023 on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047900/
1 iii.

Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate Writ, or order, or direction for further/de-novo investigation into the matter by an independent agency, preferably CBI or SIT constituted by this Hon'ble Court.

iv. Issue a writ of Quo-Warranto or any other appropriate Writ, or order, or direction to the Respondent authorities to seize the powers and removal of Respondent No.
9 and other officials of Zila Panchayat. v.

Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate Writ,
or order, or direction to Respondent authorities to initiate action against Respondent No. 7 & 8.

vi.
Issue any other writ, order or direction that this Hon'ble Court may deem fit in the interests of justice, equity and good conscience.

vii. Award the cost of the writ petition to the petitioner."
7.
The reliefs sought in the present Writ Petition, in our view, cannot be raised in a Public Interest Litigation.

Challenge has been raised to judicial orders passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Uttarkashi in Criminal Misc. Case No. 152/2023 dated 05.08.2023, and to the final report filed in Case FIR No. 01/2023, registered at PS Kotwali, Uttarkashi, under Sections 406, 409, 120B and 420 of IPC.
8.
We are, therefore, not inclined to entertain this Public Interest Litigation.

The same is,
accordingly dismissed, leaving it open to the petitioner to avail of such other remedy, as may be available to him.
9. Consequently, pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of accordingly.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) (Vipin Sanghi, C.J.) 19.10.2023 19.10.2023 Rahul WPPIL/182/2023 on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047900/
